plan.title: Discover the data
plan.question: What does one row describe, which columns are there and what does each one mean, and what do a few rows look like?
plan.expected_output: The data card read with you: the row unit, the columns grouped with their meaning and availability, and a few example rows. Nothing is decided at this step.
plan.completion: Done once a first proposal is made.

plan.title: Define the prediction moment
plan.question: At what moment is the prediction made, and what is known at that moment?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed prediction time, restated and answered in your own words.

plan.title: Decide which variables are available at prediction time
plan.question: Which variables are known at the prediction moment, and which must be excluded?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed availability status for every candidate feature, with the exclusions listed in your own words.

plan.title: Split the data before exploring it
plan.question: How are rows divided between training and validation, before any exploration of the target?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed split decision and a recorded split result.
plan.completion: Decision split is confirmed and the split result is current.

plan.title: Fix the success criterion before seeing a model
plan.question: The mean absolute error is the average size of a prediction's error, in the unit of the target. The mean baseline predicts, for every row of the validation set, the mean of the target on the training set. How much smaller than the error of the mean baseline should the validation error of the model be for it to be worth using? It is fixed now, before any model is fitted.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed minimum relative error reduction over the mean baseline, stated before any model result is seen.

plan.title: Check the structure of the data
plan.question: Which columns have missing cells, rare categories, or values outside their possible range? This check reads the development rows without the target, so the preparation decided from it comes before any look at the target.
plan.expected_output: A current quality overview of the development rows, read without the target.

plan.title: Decide how the model prepares the variables
plan.question: How should the model treat missing values, rare categories, extreme values and skewed variables? The draft reads the quality check, which does not read the target; every parameter is learnt only on the rows each model is fitted on.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed preprocessing, with the explorations that motivated it.

plan.title: Explore the target on the training rows
plan.question: What do the training rows show about the distribution of the target and the special values? Each of these analyses is a look at the target: it reads the variable to predict, and every look is counted. The preparation is already decided, before these looks.
plan.expected_output: A target summary (count, mean, standard deviation, quantiles, missing values) and special-value counts on training rows, with their exposure recorded.
plan.completion: The training EDA results are current.

plan.title: Fit a mean baseline and a linear model
plan.question: Which predictions do the training mean and a linear model give for the validation rows?
plan.expected_output: Persisted validation predictions for the mean baseline and the linear model.

plan.title: Choose the variants to compare
plan.question: Which variants of the candidate model, at most three and each with the question it answers, should be compared with it under the same evaluation: the penalty chosen by nested cross-validation, a stronger or weaker regularisation, the model without one group of variables, or another model family when the diagnostics show a pattern the linear model cannot follow?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed list of variants and their out-of-fold predictions, evaluated like the candidate.
plan.completion: Decision model_variant is confirmed and every variant fit is current.

plan.title: Choose the model
plan.question: Does the linear model reduce the validation error of the mean baseline, in the target unit, by enough to adopt it, given the paired intervals and the residuals?
plan.expected_output: A current regression evaluation and a confirmed model choice.
plan.completion: The regression evaluation is current and decision model_choice is confirmed.

plan.title: Open the final test once
plan.question: Now that the model is chosen, do you open the sealed final test, once, to measure it on rows nothing has seen? After this, any change is made after the final test.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed opening in your own words, and the one evaluation of the chosen configuration on the final test.
plan.completion: Decision final_test is confirmed and the final evaluation is recorded.

plan.title: Conclude proportionately
plan.question: What can be said, for which use, and with which limits? Keeping the baseline is a valid result.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed conclusion that names its limits.

coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects. The fit is penalised: its coefficients are pulled towards zero, so the intervals describe the spread of the penalised estimate, centred on a value that is itself shrunk; they are not exact confidence intervals of an unpenalised coefficient, and a coefficient of a rare category can be shrunk well inside its interval.
